title: 写作与表达：诗的技艺 — Day 31
title_en: Writing & Expression: The Craft of Poetry — Day 31

questions.question: 文中用认知心理学的生成效应来说明留白为何有力：自己补出来的东西记得更牢。它同时由此推出了留白的什么限制？
options: 生成效应只对诗歌有效，所以商务写作里不该使用留白
读者自己补出的结论往往不被信任，所以要再补一句总结
留白越多读者参与越深，所以应当尽量把所有结论都留给读者自己
读者补错了也会记得牢，所以留白必须精确，缝只能留一道
questions.explanation: 文章说生成效应证明的是记得牢，不是信得过：读者补错了同样会记得牢。所以留白必须是精确地省略，不是含糊其辞，你心里那个字必须先在，才谈得上不写它。留得越多越好恰恰是它要防的方向。
questions.question_en: The article cites the generation effect — people remember better what they fill in themselves — to explain why leaving things unsaid works. What limit on leaving things out does it draw from the same effect?
options_en: The generation effect only works for poetry, so business writing should not leave things unsaid
Readers tend to distrust conclusions they reached themselves, so a summary line should be added
The more you leave out, the deeper readers engage, so conclusions should be left to them wherever possible
A reader who fills the gap wrongly will remember it just as well, so the omission must be precise and narrow
questions.explanation_en: The article notes that the generation effect proves memorability, not trustworthiness: a reader who fills the gap wrongly remembers the error just as firmly. So leaving out must be precise omission, not vagueness; the word you leave unwritten has to exist in your mind first. "The more left out the better" is exactly the direction it warns against.

questions.question: 写作中给自己设约束（字数上限、只放一句话的 slide）可以逼出创造，但也可能退化成八股。文章给的分界线是什么？
options: 约束是否足够严格，越严苛越能逼出好作品，太宽松的约束才会僵化
约束是否出自古典格律传统，自创的规则更容易沦为空洞模板
约束是否还在逼你取舍、帮你思考，而不是满足它本身成了目的
约束是否被团队里的所有人共同遵守，各行其是时才会出问题
questions.explanation: 文章说分界在于约束服务于谁：逼你做取舍、把想法磨利时它是杠杆；当凑字数、套模板、为对仗扭曲意思成了目的，它就是八股。健康的约束是难而有意义，僵死的约束是易而无意义。人人套同一个模板，正是它举的退化例子。
questions.question_en: Setting yourself constraints in writing (a word limit, one sentence per slide) can force creativity, but can also decay into formula. What dividing line does the article give?
options_en: Whether the constraint is strict enough, since harsher rules force better work and only loose ones ossify
Whether the constraint comes from classical verse tradition, since home-made rules decay into templates more easily
Whether the constraint still forces trade-offs and helps you think, rather than satisfying it becoming the goal
Whether everyone on the team follows the constraint together, since trouble only starts when people diverge
questions.explanation_en: The article says the line is whom the constraint serves: when it forces choices and sharpens ideas it is leverage; when padding to a count, fitting a template or twisting meaning for parallelism becomes the point, it is formula. Healthy constraints are hard and meaningful; dead ones are easy and meaningless. Everyone using the same template is its own example of decay.

questions.question: 在设计文档里写「这个系统像一只漏水的桶」，生动好记。按文章的看法，这类意象在技术写作里该放在哪里？
options: 意象比数字更容易被记住，所以论证的关键处也应优先用意象
技术文档要求无歧义，所以任何意象都不该出现在设计文档里
意象只适合放在结尾留白，让读者自己推出该采取什么措施
用意象点燃动机、引人读下去，正文论证要回到漏率这样的数字
questions.explanation: 文章在「推到边界」里说，意象的力量在唤起共同经验，但技术文档要的是无歧义，「漏水的桶」不能替代漏率的数字。规律是用意象点燃动机，用数字承载论证：开头一个画面让人想读下去，正文回到精确，位置搞反就是灾难。它没有说技术文档完全不能用意象。
questions.question_en: Writing "this system is like a leaky bucket" in a design document is vivid and memorable. Where does the article say such imagery belongs in technical writing?
options_en: Images are remembered better than numbers, so the key points of the argument should also lead with imagery
Technical documents require zero ambiguity, so no imagery of any kind belongs in a design document
Imagery belongs only in the closing gap, letting readers infer for themselves what action to take
Use the image to spark interest and draw readers in, while the argument itself rests on numbers like the leak rate
questions.explanation_en: In its closing reflections the article says imagery works by evoking shared experience, but technical documents need precision, and a leaky bucket cannot replace the leak rate. The rule: images to spark motivation, numbers to carry the argument — an opening picture to draw readers in, then back to precision; reversing them is a disaster. It does not ban imagery from technical writing outright.
